mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary and subsequent legalization by the Egyptian Consulate or Embassy in the shareholder's country; no Hague Apostille available because Egypt is not a Contracting Party to the Apostille Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory protocol requires screening of each shareholder, manager, legal representative and 25% plus ultimate beneficial owner against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Egyptian AMLCFTU domestic terrorist and sanctions list, and a licensed international PEP database. Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory under the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification issued for Interactive Audio Chatroom and Companion Social Applications, including independent source-of-funds and source-of-wealth corroboration, senior-management approval of UBO confirmation, and continuous sanctions re-screening. The Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority and GAFI retain audit rights over the CDD file for a minimum of five years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Online Corporate Name Reservation and E-Registration Portal, accessible through GAFI's official website and the unified digital investment platform of Egypt
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be composed in Arabic script and must be registered in Arabic as the controlling legal name. A foreign-language trade name may be recorded in the commercial register only after the Arabic name is cleared and the Arabic transliteration is adopted. For an Interactive Audio Chatroom and Companion Social Application, the name must not imply sectoral licensing terms such as broadcasting, telecommunications or financial services unless the relevant regulator's approval is uploaded, and the name must not be misleading, incongruent with the ISIC 6311 activity, or similar to a previously reserved or registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government / State / Republic / Ministry / Official / Sovereign
words or expressions contrary to public order, national security, public morals or religious sanctity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon administrative rejection of a name, the applicant may file an online grievance with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within ten working days from the electronic rejection notice, supplying a legal memorandum and an alternative Arabic name. GAFI must issue a reasoned decision within fifteen working days. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may appeal to the competent Administrative Court of the State Council within sixty days from the notification of the reasoning, while simultaneously submitting a new name reservation request to GAFI.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office is not accepted as the statutory registered address of an Egyptian LLC engaged in voice streaming and audio companion services. The company must maintain a physical commercial address in Egypt capable of receiving process, housing statutory records and enabling inspection by GAFI, tax authorities and AML/CFT supervisors. A managed or serviced business centre is acceptable only if the provider is licensed, a private desk or room is dedicated, the company name is displayed, and law enforcement / supervisory authorities are granted unimpeded physical access. A P.O. Box, single-mail receptor or remote-only virtual address does not satisfy the commercial substance requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 30% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first twelve months after commercial registration, increasing to 45% in the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and for non-resident-managed companies. GAFI, municipal licensing officers and the Egyptian Tax Authority may perform unannounced site visits to verify the nameplate, lease contract or ownership document, presence of management, physical staff capacity and bona fide continuity of the voice-streaming business.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended (Government of Egypt), notably Articles 46 through 94 concerning Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (GAFI Unified Investment Procedures); Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration and Commercial Registry Directorate, Cairo.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Request for Incorporation and Articles of Association (Uqd Ta'sis) submitted through the GAFI Investor Services Portal and authenticated by a notary public.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an LLC under the direct investment regime; the capital is set in the Articles of Association and must be fully deposited into a temporary bank account before registration unless wholly in-kind, in which case a bank certificate of audit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation application and Articles of Association submitted by the subscribers be and hereby are ratified and approved. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Registered Office of the Company be fixed at its declared address in Cairo, Egypt, and the Company is authorized to establish branch registrations as required by the authorities. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Directors duly elected hereunder be authorized to purchase, lease, and equip the technical infrastructure for the licensed voice-streaming application. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the undersigned Directors are appointed as the first Board of Directors and the Chairman; the Chairman and any one Director are authorized to execute all applications with GAFI, tax, labor, and data-protection authorities and to appoint the initial auditors and bank signatories.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry Directorate (online via GAFI Investor Services Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three Arabic and two English candidate names through the GAFI portal; verify absence of identical or confusingly similar registered names and obtain a provisional name certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed name-search request form
Clear copy of founding partners' passports or national ID
Digital copy of the intended Articles of Association for preliminary review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, file a written objection with GAFI Commercial Registry within 15 days and resubmit alternative names at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Dar El Selh) and GAFI Legal Validation Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic-language Articles of Association in GAFI's model form, have all founding partners appear before a notary public, execute the document, and obtain notarized certified copies for filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
Legally leased registered-office contract (or proof of property title)
Signed ID/passport copies of all founding partners
Power of attorney if any partner acts by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: GAFI legal officers may issue a 'Formalities Correction Sheet'; correct the deficiency and resubmit within 30 days to preserve the original submission priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and bank certificate issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian licensed commercial bank operating under Central Bank of Egypt supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-escrow bank account in the company's name, deposit the capital stated in the Articles of Association, and obtain a certified bank certificate evidencing that 100% of the capital is in the account or is represented by audited in-kind contributions.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
GAFI provisional incorporation file number
Administered ID/passport of the legal representative
Registration form opened the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit due to AML/CTF customer-due-diligence concerns, provide supplemental source-of-wealth documentation or request a substitute bank through GAFI's banking-support desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Office (One-Stop Invest Center)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized Articles, bank certificate, address lease, and valid IDs into the GAFI portal; pay the statutory registration and publication fees; and receive the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Qayd Al-Tijari).
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation application (signed form)
Notarized Articles of Association and original interim name certificate
Bank capital-deposit certificate
Original registered-office lease and recent utility receipt
Photographs and passports of all managers/partners
Ownership declaration for any in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI queries the application, correct the specific noted deficiency or objection within 30 days; administrative appeals are decided by GAFI's Internal Appeals Committee within 15 days, followed by the Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, social insurance, and labor registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), General Authority for Social Insurance (GASI), and local Ministry of Labor office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the GAFI One-Stop post-registration service to register the company for Corporate Tax, VAT, payroll, social insurance for staff, and the labor force office; obtain a unified tax card after physical inspection or e-verification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and commercial registration extract
Notarized Articles of Association
Lease agreement and electricity/utility bill
Director and representative national IDs/passports
Employment contracts of initial staff and pension forms PSA/F3
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card is delayed, request a provisional temporary tax card from ETA under Article 34 of Income Tax Law 91/2005; the card must be issued within five working days after verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data protection and digital-service ancillary registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Data Protection Authority (NDPA) in coordination with Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a data controller and, if applicable, the voice-streaming service's data-processing description under Law No. 151 of 2020; file the mandatory data-protection notification before commencing operations, and adopt binding appointment of a Data Protection Officer (DPO).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Unified tax card
Data-protection registration form and privacy policy
DPO appointment letter and professional credential list
Standard technical/cloud infrastructure specification and third-party processor list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NDPA requests additional technical security descriptions, provide an updated information-security annex; any refusal of registration may be appealed to the NDPA executive office within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – exempt from industrial operating license under Article 9 of Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 for purely non-manufacturing digital services; if physical server/equipment assembly is later conducted, the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) would become competent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – Digital Service Activity Exemption (Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017, Art. 9); GAFI and NDPA approvals constitute the operational authorization for the voice-streaming application.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) in conjunction with the Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Exempted / Minimal Impact for server-hosting and software-application operations; no mandatory EIA disclosure is required absent the physical construction of a cloud-data-center facility with installed transformer capacity exceeding 2 MVA or floor area above 5,000 m².
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 for the Environment and its amending Law No. 202 of 2020: no direct industrial wastewater or VOC emissions from software operations; wastewater from staff facilities must be discharged to municipal sewers within Egyptian Effluent Discharge Standards (ECP 501/2015); e-waste including replaced server batteries and electronic boards must be handled under Waste Regulation Law No. 202 of 2020 with registered recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval from the Civil Defense Authority of the Egyptian Ministry of Interior confirming appropriate automatic fire suppression in any server or office premises; structural load inspection certificate from the Cairo Governmental Engineering Administration for any hosting-floor load; and occupational safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower under Occupational Safety and Health Law No. 12 of 2003.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt; unified e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipts clearance portal: https://eservices.invoicing.eta.gov.eg; investment licensing via GAFI One-Stop-Shop.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate EG_LLC with GAFI One-Stop-Shop and obtain the Commercial Register certificate. Step 2: File the Income Tax file opening form (Form 202) at the competent ETA tax office to obtain the Tax Card (TIN). Step 3: Apply for VAT registration under Law No. 67/2016 and obtain a separate VAT Registration Number (mandatory within 60 days of exceeding EGP 500,000 annual taxable supplies; voluntary registration permitted below threshold). Step 4: Onboard to the ETA e-invoicing platform: register authorized signatories, obtain MFA credentials and digital signing certificates, and validate XML/JSON invoice schema. Non-resident ownership is permitted with no minimum capital; the foreign-invested LLC must obtain its ETA TIN before commencing operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — opaque resident taxpayer. EG_LLC is subject to Egyptian corporate income tax at 22.5% on worldwide income under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended. No pass-through treatment; shareholders are taxed separately on distributions. Non-resident entities are taxed on Egypt-source income only. Not within a tax-exempt zone regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no check-the-box or hybrid entity classification election; statutory legal form is conclusive for tax classification. Available elections include: (i) voluntary VAT registration below the mandatory threshold; (ii) selection of the fiscal year with ETA approval; (iii) simplified quarterly VAT registration and filing for non-resident digital-supply suppliers; (iv) Advance Pricing Agreement applications for transfer-pricing certainty. Hybrid mismatch elective regimes under OECD BEPS Action 2 have not been enacted in Egypt.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by Law No. 3 of 2022 (electronic and digital services) and Executive Regulation No. 66 of 2017
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: EGP 500,000 annual taxable supplies. Voluntary registration: available for taxable persons below the mandatory threshold. Non-resident suppliers of digital services (including streaming and in-app downloadable content) are subject to a simplified ETA registration and quarterly filing regime when their taxable supplies consumed in Egypt exceed the prescribed threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipts for all VAT-registered taxpayers. Invoices are transmitted in real time to the ETA focal-clearance system via RESTful APIs in XML/JSON; each invoice receives a unique UUID and QR code and is cleared before legal issuance. B2C in-app transactions through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing must be supported by e-receipts where the end user is in the Egyptian storefront. Non-compliance suspends invoice clearing and attracts penalties of EGP 20,000–100,000, potential business closure, and revocation of e-invoicing privileges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of services are zero-rated under Article 13 of VAT Law No. 67/2016 where the service is rendered to a non-resident recipient having no permanent establishment in Egypt and the service is performed and consumed outside Egypt. Voice-streaming and audio-chat revenues derived through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing qualify as exported services when the applicable storefront and billing territory are outside Egypt and proceeds are received in foreign currency. Egyptian-storefront sales are subject to 14% VAT (platform merchant-of-record collection may apply).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (statutory for goods; for pure digital services the ETA accepts zero-rated service export invoices and annual digital-service export declarations in lieu of customs filing)

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (goods) — replaced for streaming exports by Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console payout reports evidencing digital delivery to non-resident storefronts and gross sales per territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Egyptian bank, or equivalent FX credit advice, evidencing hard-currency settlement from Apple/Google credited to an Egyptian bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may audit zero-rating claims within the statutory assessment period; deficient substantiation triggers reversal of the 0% rate, assessment of 14% VAT, a monthly late-payment addition of 2% of the unpaid VAT under Article 90 of Law No. 67/2016, and fines of EGP 5,000–50,000 for documentation violations. Knowingly false export documentation constitutes tax evasion under Law No. 177 of 2022, carrying imprisonment and a fine of double to five times the evaded tax, cancellation of VAT registration, and inadmissibility of the purported inward remittance as export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020. The CBE regulates licensed banks, foreign-exchange dealers, payment systems, payment service providers, and foreign-exchange transactions. The Egyptian Customs Authority, the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), and the Egyptian Tax Authority also control documentation relevant to cross-border capital, trade, and tax remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound is not freely convertible in the manner of a fully open capital-account currency. Current-account payments, including legitimate imports, exported services, software and technology payments, dividends, interest, royalties, and other business remittances, are generally processed through licensed Egyptian banks subject to documentary evidence, sanctions screening, tax compliance, and available foreign currency liquidity. Capital-account transactions, including foreign investment, capital reductions, shareholder loans, and intercompany funding, require enhanced documentation and may require GAFI, CBE, bank, corporate-registry, or sector-specific approvals. A foreign-owned LLC may generally receive foreign capital and remit distributable profits, but remittance is not automatic: the bank normally requires audited or approved financial statements, shareholder or board resolutions, tax-clearance or tax-compliance evidence, evidence that the profits are legally distributable, proof of payment of applicable Egyptian withholding tax, and evidence of the original investment or funding trail. Dividend and service-fee remittances can be delayed by foreign-currency availability, correspondent-bank controls, incomplete beneficial-owner information, inconsistent commercial invoices, transfer-pricing concerns, sanctions screening, or unresolved tax filings. Mobile-app receipts from Apple and Google are cross-border service or platform receipts and should be supported by platform statements, contractual terms, settlement reports, bank advices, and accounting records. No assumption should be made that local revenues may be converted or transferred offshore without bank review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egypt does not generally impose a universal statutory requirement that all export proceeds be surrendered to the banking system at a fixed mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters are expected to use licensed banks for foreign-exchange transactions and to satisfy applicable customs, banking, and trade-documentation requirements. For goods, export proceeds and customs records must be capable of reconciliation, and the collecting bank may require evidence of shipment, invoices, bills of lading, customs declarations, and receipt of funds. For digital services and app-platform receipts, the company should retain platform contracts, monthly settlement statements, invoices or equivalent revenue records, remittance advices, and evidence of the underlying service. Applicable CBE instructions, bank procedures, customs rules, and future emergency measures may impose reporting, repatriation, or documentary requirements; therefore, no fixed statutory repatriation deadline or mandatory conversion percentage should be recorded without confirmation from the relationship bank for the relevant transaction. Foreign currency may generally be retained in an authorized foreign-currency account, subject to bank policy and applicable CBE rules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to Low for primary treasury banking and Low for unlicensed offshore EMI substitution. An offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide Egyptian payment, deposit-taking, local collection, local acquiring, or domestic settlement services merely because the company holds an offshore account. Payment services in Egypt are regulated under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 and related CBE rules; local payment acceptance, wallet services, acquiring, payment aggregation, and domestic settlement generally require a CBE-licensed bank or payment-system/payment-service provider. Offshore EMIs may be used for limited corporate treasury functions where the Egyptian bank, the EMI, and the correspondent banks accept the structure, but the company must preserve a licensed Egyptian bank account for statutory payments, payroll, taxes, local expenses, capital documentation, and regulated FX transactions. Apple and Google settlement arrangements require reconciliation to the Egyptian entity's books and may be challenged if the payee entity, contracting entity, tax residence, or beneficial owner is inconsistent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal rule requiring every director to appear physically at every Egyptian bank. However, banks commonly require in-person attendance or a live video interview for authorized signatories, beneficial owners, and foreign shareholders, particularly for newly incorporated foreign-owned entities, foreign-currency accounts, high-risk digital businesses, or unusual cross-border flows. Remote onboarding may be accepted at the bank's discretion after notarization, legalization, apostille where applicable, certified Arabic translation, embassy authentication where required, and satisfactory verification through independent sources. The bank may require an Egyptian-resident authorized signatory, a local office visit, specimen-signature verification, original corporate documents, and refreshed KYC after changes in ownership or control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-owned LLC with an unclear ultimate beneficial owner, nominee shareholders, layered offshore ownership, or inconsistent ownership information across GAFI, commercial-register, tax, and bank records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents; current commercial-register extract; GAFI incorporation and investment documents; complete ownership chart to natural persons; passports and proof of address for all beneficial owners and controllers; director and authorized-signatory resolutions; independent corporate-registry extracts for intermediate entities; beneficial-owner declaration; sanctions and politically exposed person screening record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Voice-streaming or social-app activity viewed as elevated risk because of user-generated content, anonymous users, virtual gifts, creator payouts, minors, online abuse, fraud, or possible money-laundering through platform balances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and funds-flow memorandum; terms of service; prohibited-content and acceptable-use policies; age-gating and child-safety controls; user and merchant onboarding controls; transaction-monitoring rules; chargeback and refund procedures; suspicious-activity escalation matrix; creator and payout due-diligence procedures; platform moderation policy; data-retention and audit-log description; independent compliance contact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from Apple or Google paid into an account or by an entity that differs from the Egyptian LLC named in corporate, tax, or banking documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform agreements; app-store developer-account ownership evidence; tax forms submitted to the platform; monthly sales and settlement reports; invoices or settlement statements; bank remittance advices; intercompany agreement if another group entity contracts with the platform; transfer-pricing analysis; board approval; accounting reconciliation linking gross user receipts, platform commissions, taxes, refunds, and net remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or irregular inbound shareholder funding described as a loan, capital contribution, advance, or service payment without consistent legal characterization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolution; capital-increase or loan agreement; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; lender and borrower corporate documents; funding schedule; repayment and interest terms; GAFI or registry filings where applicable; bank purpose classification; tax analysis; transfer-pricing support; SWIFT message and originating-account evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to foreign affiliates, licensors, cloud providers, marketing agencies, or developers with weak commercial substance or incomplete tax treatment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed agreement; invoice; deliverables and acceptance evidence; purchase order; beneficial-owner and sanctions checks; withholding-tax analysis; treaty-residence certificate where treaty relief is claimed; transfer-pricing benchmarking; board or management approval; bank payment application; evidence of receipt by the contractual beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested foreign-currency remittance despite unpaid Egyptian taxes, missing tax filings, unexplained retained earnings, or insufficient distributable-profit evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements; trial balance and retained-earnings schedule; shareholder dividend resolution; tax returns; tax-clearance or tax-compliance certificate where requested; withholding-tax payment receipt; statutory accounts; bank statements; proof of source of distributable funds; legal confirmation that the remittance is not a prohibited capital reduction or disguised distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unlicensed payment intermediaries, crypto exchanges, cash-intensive channels, or unrelated third-party settlement accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal remediation plan; prohibition policy; corrected commercial payment instructions; complete transaction reconstruction; counterparty KYC; source-of-funds evidence; management explanation; bank-approved collection and payout flow; enhanced monitoring undertaking; evidence that future settlements will use licensed banks or authorized payment providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among the ISIC classification, commercial activity, app functionality, website, licensing position, and expected transaction profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business-plan memorandum; app demonstration; technical architecture; revenue model; customer and supplier map; confirmation that no regulated lending, deposit-taking, remittance, gambling, securities, telecom, or payment activity is conducted without authorization; GAFI and commercial-register activity descriptions; legal opinion on licensing perimeter; projected monthly transaction profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity through a CBE-regulated Egyptian bank into a designated foreign-currency or capital account using the exact legal name of the Egyptian LLC and the originating shareholder's account. Before transfer, provide the bank with the incorporation documents, commercial-register extract, GAFI investment file, shareholder resolution, capital-increase or funding agreement, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, expected amount and currency, and intended purpose. The bank should assign the applicable CBE or internal transaction-purpose classification; no invented purpose code should be used where the bank has not confirmed the code. The SWIFT message should identify the investment or shareholder-loan purpose accurately and avoid generic descriptions such as 'consulting' or 'payment.' For a capital increase, complete the required corporate and registry filings and preserve the bank certificate evidencing receipt of capital. For a shareholder loan, execute the loan agreement before funding, document interest and maturity, analyze Egyptian withholding tax and transfer pricing, and confirm whether any GAFI, CBE, registry, or bank notification is required. Reconcile the incoming amount to the accounting ledger, foreign-investment records, and beneficial-owner file. Do not route capital through Apple, Google, unrelated affiliates, personal accounts, cash, or unlicensed payment intermediaries.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the Egyptian LLC's licensed-bank account and pay the named contractual beneficiary through a bank-supported SWIFT wire, normally an MT103 or its current ISO 20022 equivalent, with a precise payment purpose, invoice number, contract reference, beneficiary banking details, and charge allocation. For higher-value or documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a licensed bank, with invoice, packing list, transport document, insurance document, certificate of origin, customs documentation, and inspection documents where applicable. Documentary collection, open-account settlement, and advance payment may be available subject to bank policy, counterparty risk, import and customs rules, and CBE documentation requirements. For software, cloud, hosting, app-store, advertising, content, and professional-service payments, retain the agreement, invoice, proof of performance, tax analysis, withholding-tax evidence, and beneficiary KYC; these payments are not automatically 'trade imports' merely because they are cross-border. The bank may request import or service documentation, tax forms, sanctions screening, and evidence of foreign-currency availability. Maintain a three-way reconciliation among contract, invoice, and bank payment, and retain SWIFT confirmation and beneficiary receipt evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a CBE-authorized bank, generally limited by bank policy to a documented underlying exposure, approved tenor, counterparty limits, and evidence of expected receivables or payables.

Foreign-exchange swaps with a licensed Egyptian bank for liquidity and maturity management, subject to CBE rules, bank treasury limits, documented underlying exposure, and appropriate accounting and valuation controls.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available only where offered and permitted by a licensed bank under applicable CBE rules and the bank's approved product framework. Availability, currencies, eligible counterparties, collateral, settlement method, and documentation must be confirmed in writing; an NDF must not be used to evade Egyptian FX controls.

Plain-vanilla currency options or option-based hedges may be available from authorized banks subject to product approval, suitability, underlying exposure, disclosure of premium and contingent obligations, and treasury risk limits.

Operational controls should include a board-approved treasury policy, delegated dealing authority, counterparty limits, hedge-designation records, exposure forecasts, independent valuation, confirmation matching, collateral monitoring, and prohibition of speculative positions unrelated to identifiable business exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 41) with tax computations covering income from voice streaming, in-app purchase merchant fees, and related ancillary revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Corporate Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 2% per month (or fraction of a month) on the differential tax amount, minimum EGP 500 (approx. USD 10), interest on late payment, enforced collection, and potential criminal proceedings for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited annual financial statements and activity report submitted as the annual corporate filing to the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registry / One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general assembly must approve the accounts within 6 months of the fiscal year end; audited statements must be filed with GAFI within 30 days of approval (practical outer date of 7 months after year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI late-filing fines, suspension of company certificates and official extracts, and, for persistent non-compliance, compulsory strike-off or liquidation proceedings under Companies Law No. 194 of 2020.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) register confirmation and any ownership-change filing caused by share transfers during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Beneficial Ownership Registry and the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual UBO confirmation filed concurrently with the GAFI annual accounts filing; any share transfer altering ultimate control must be reported within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000 (approx. USD 10–100) per month of delay under the AML executive regulations, blockage of GAFI transactional approvals, and added AML examination risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tax Card (taxpayer registration identification card) biennial renewal and validation of the corporate tax file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Taxpayer Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal every 2 years from the date of issuance; for a newly incorporated entity, first renewal falls at the end of the second calendar year of operation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inability to execute contracts requiring notarization, customs clearance, public-sector tenders, or banking formalities; delay penalties and possible freezing of the tax file for prolonged non-renewal.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for every Egyptian LLC without any revenue, asset, or headcount exemption; the company must appoint at least one certified auditor licensed and enrolled in the Egyptian Accountants' and Auditors' Register, with mandatory rotation after the legally prescribed maximum tenure.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially aligned with IFRS; full IFRS is required for entities listed on the Egyptian Exchange, while non-listed LLCs apply EAS as issued by the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a current beneficial ownership register and reconfirm its contents at each annual GAFI filing cycle; any share transfer that changes ultimate control requires an amended UBO filing within 30 days of the transfer registration, and the members' register must record each transfer before such filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–600 per year for a commercial registered office arrangement in Cairo or Alexandria, inclusive of corporate agent and GAFI interface services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–6,000 per year depending on streaming revenue volume, payout-data reconciliation across Apple IAP and Google Play Billing rails, and tax-review engagement depth

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt imposes no general tax holiday for an ordinary LLC. Baseline effective rate is 22.5% on taxable income after ordinary deductions. Under Investment Law No. 72/2017, qualifying projects in promoted sectors may deduct up to 50% of investable costs against taxable income for up to five years; free-zone entities may enjoy 0% CIT on qualifying export and logistics activity. Small and micro businesses electing Law No. 152/2020 may pay 0.5%–1.5% of gross turnover instead of the standard CIT regime. The voice-streaming app business is presumed in the standard 22.5% regime absent an approved Investment Law incentive certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 2 (Corporate Income Tax Return) submitted through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at www.eta.gov.eg, supported by audited financial statements and the annual transfer pricing disclosure annex.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly preliminary tax payments are required during the year, with monthly withholding tax and e-invoice obligations running in parallel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and self-assessed tax balance must be filed within four months after the close of the company's fiscal/tax year. For a 31 December year-end, the deadline is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: entity legal name, commercial registration number, tax card number, registered address, taxpayer category, and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian LLC's identification data only. Non-resident shareholder details are captured in the related-party disclosure annex rather than in Box 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Activity classification: main ISIC activity code and narrative description of the interactive audio chatroom and companion social application services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the Egyptian operational scope precisely; if the foreign parent sells only technical services into Egypt, annotate the absence of a permanent establishment in the explanatory notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: full gross receipts from voice streaming, in-app purchases, subscriptions, and ancillary advertising, recognised under Egyptian GAAP on a gross basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payout statements to Egyptian bank receipts; no net-of-store-fee reporting is permitted absent prior ETA acceptance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and operating expenses: platform commission fees, content licensing, bandwidth, salaries, rent, depreciation, marketing, and general administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border recharge invoices from the foreign parent or group must be supported by transfer pricing documentation; disallowed items such as entertainment, fines, and foreign taxes paid in lieu of Egyptian tax are added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net profit before tax extracted from the audited Egyptian statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian statutory ledger is the primary tax basis; intra-group royalty or service loadings that distort the Egyptian profit are challenged and re-characterised.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: timing differences for depreciation and amortisation recomputation, capitalisation of software development, provisions disallowance, and other permanent differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply ETA-recognised useful lives for platform software and technology assets; maintain a contemporaneous fixed-asset register for non-resident auditors and ETA inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward: offset of prior-year losses within the statutory five-year carryforward limit, subject to ownership and activity continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Egyptian LLC's own losses may be carried forward; foreign parent or group losses are not transferable into the Egyptian tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all adjustments and the resultant corporate income tax computed at 22.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-based reductions of Egyptian source income are recognised only after the ETA International Taxation department approves the DTA relief application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and prepayments: wage withholding tax, dividend withholding credits, tax withheld by third parties, and quarterly advance instalments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits must be traceable to ETA payment receipts in the LLC's name; non-resident shareholders cannot claim credits through this return for taxes borne offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final computation: net tax payable after credits or refund due from the ETA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund is payable to the Egyptian bank account of the LLC; subsequent dividend remittances to non-residents are independently subject to the 10% dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 per return under Law 91/2005. Late payment of assessed tax accrues a 3% monthly delay surcharge on the unpaid balance, generally capped at 100% of the tax under ETA circular practice. Failure to issue e-invoices in the mandatory electronic invoicing system adds up to EGP 50,000 per violation. Material understatement with fraudulent intent shifts the case to criminal tax prosecution involving double tax fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% domestic withholding tax, imposed as a final tax on cash or in-kind dividend distributions by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders under Article 57 of Law No. 91/2005. Domestic law reductions may apply to certain Egyptian corporate recipients, but non-resident individuals and companies generally face the full 10% unless a tax treaty provides otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Egyptian paying LLC: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the relevant calendar year issued by the treaty jurisdiction's tax authority, duly attested or apostilled as required by ETA practice; (ii) a completed DTA relief application form containing identity, ownership, and income details; and (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient has no Egyptian permanent establishment and is not a conduit. The LLC submits the package to the ETA International Taxation department before effecting payment at the reduced rate. If the treaty rate is applied pending approval, the ETA may later demand the shortfall; where withholding was made at the statutory 10% and treaty relief is later accepted, the excess is recoverable through the ETA refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 20% withholding on gross royalties, technical service fees and interest paid by an Egyptian LLC to a non-resident lacking a PEP. Under Egyptian double taxation agreements, treaty ceilings commonly range from 10% to 15% for interest and from 12% to 15% for royalties, depending on the counterparty treaty and the beneficial ownership conditions. The same TRC plus beneficial-owner protocol governs entitlement to the reduced treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 5 million: aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions trigger a mandatory Local File. EGP 50 million: aggregate annual related-party transactions trigger a mandatory Master File. These thresholds apply under ETA Resolutions No. 51/2019 and subsequent amending resolutions; the annual CIT return must include a transfer pricing disclosure schedule identifying controlled transactions, counterparties, methods selected and the arm's length outcome.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute comparable to GCC regimes. Nevertheless, the ETA applies substance-over-form principles and a general anti-avoidance rule under Article 111 of Law No. 91/2005, requiring that the Egyptian LLC demonstrate real commercial activity, local management, staff and independent decision-making. A foreign streaming principal with significant local digital activity, servers or dependent agents may be deemed to have a taxable permanent establishment even absent a registered branch. Free-zone subsidiaries must maintain genuine activity to justify continued 0% CIT treatment and may lose the benefit upon a sham-substance finding.
